title: 0014-search-authorized-encrypted-credential-values.md
body_text:
# ADR 0014: Search authorized encrypted credential values server-side

Date: 2026-07-13  
Status: accepted

## Context

The Credentials page needs backend search by record title, visible login, and dynamic fields. Dynamic-field values are encrypted at rest and are intentionally absent from list projections. Searching only client-visible metadata cannot find records by those values, while placing a potentially secret search string in a GET URL risks exposing it through request URLs, history, diagnostics, or infrastructure logs.

## Decision

Provide a dedicated project-scoped `POST /api/projects/:projectId/credentials/search` operation with a strictly validated body and `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The shared Credentials application service first resolves the actor's active project membership, `credentials.view` permission, and category grants exactly as the normal list operation does. It considers only active credentials from those visible categories. For matching, the service normalizes the query and compares it case-insensitively with the credential title, decrypted login, dynamic-field label, and decrypted dynamic-field value.

The response remains the existing safe list projection. It may contain the login allowed by ADR 0011, but never contains passwords or dynamic-field values. Search queries and decrypted comparison values must not enter logs, analytics, audit metadata, caches, indexes, MCP, or client persistence. Empty searches continue to use the normal list endpoint. Client requests are debounced and superseded searches are aborted.

## Consequences

- Authorized users can locate credentials by information stored in encrypted dynamic fields without adding a plaintext database index.
- Search cost is linear in the actor's accessible active credentials and dynamic fields because encrypted values cannot use ordinary database substring indexes.
- A matching result reveals that an accessible credential contains the supplied text even though the dynamic-field value itself is not returned. This is limited to users already authorized to view that credential category.
- Search remains excluded from MCP and must be revisited before introducing large credential collections, external indexing, or broader reveal permissions.
